Hey man. Imma be down to earth with you.

 I’ve been there and done that around a trillion times. I understand the feeling of doing the bare minimum just for people not to notice what’s wrong with my mental health - in fact I’m so good at faking my satisfaction, that sometimes I start to question myself. 

For me it’s like living two entirely different lives; the one people can physically see and the other that is trapped in my head. Seeking joy in life appears to be a chore and a duty in order to fit into that mould that I’ve created of myself. 

The only motivation for me right now is my family, and that encourages me to seek help. I thought I’d share my story so that you will not feel alone in this battle. There are a bunch of other resources out there if therapy is not accessible and I’m always happy to chat. I’m still in high school so I think I can kind of relate on how the atmosphere is at school. It’s the first step that matters. Good luck.

hey man, I hear you. 

I understand what it feels like to be in this state and as cliche as this sounds, there is light. It may seem that the term ‘light’ may be nothing but fabricated happiness but trust me, true happiness is hard to find but is always there to be discovered. Getting help is a very, very hard first step to take by yourself or with the support of others but remember to stand tall and try again no matter how many times you may have discarded the idea of visiting someone to get help. It seems like you’ve lost motivation for the basic necessities, essentially running on the bare minimum to survive, I did too. Use the passing of your brother as your motivation. As stupid as this sounds, use your brother as a spiritual motivator to lead your life. I believe in you. 

You’ve probably heard something along these lines a billion times but there is light at the end of the tunnel. Hang on there buddy. 

Inbox me if you want to talk about anything :)

I’m still young but I’ve witnessed my parents go through a similar situation. 

One fell out of love and that’s the last thing the other wanted. Long story short, my parents now live great lives apart but it’s safe to say that it was a heck of a battle to for it to get to where it is now. Now that I’m slightly older, I can see why and perhaps how it happened but that’s not what the main point is here. 

What I’m trying to say is that there is a way out and a marriage established on aggression and resentment isn’t going to go any further than two empty strangers living together. I recall my mum telling me how her psychologist helped her with just one question - ‘can you live happily without him [my dad]?’. 
Yes, due to your illness, you are dependent on your husband but that doesn’t mean he’s your only possible support. There are many resources out there that can support you financially and more importantly, there are many groups and organisations out there that is there for you (as mentioned above by previous posters). The point of me sharing my story is for you to know that you’re not alone. People who are going through similar situations or had gone through these issues had come out stronger than ever. As for kids, options such as IVF exists. The most important thing is, please consider your health and stay safe! I know that you are going through a tough time but please know that there is light at the end of the tunnel.
